description: Students advance their German language skills through engagement with texts concerning the effects
of the past on the present. Topics include protest and resistance, environmental sustainability,
and exile experiences, as captured in a graphic novel, short stories, essays, songs, and film.
Close reading and integrated grammar and vocabulary-building tasks allow students to improve their
German comprehension, speaking and writing. They develop critical literacy skills through written
reflections and essays, and interpersonal, interpretive, and presentational speaking tasks. Taught
in German. Offered annually in the spring semester.  Prerequisite: GERM 231 or by placement test.
